MPs who sponsor lobbyists’ entry to halls of power will also be listed online under new transparency rules Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Political lobbyists with unfettered access to the halls of Parliament House – and the MPs who sponsor their passes – will soon be publicly identified in an online register, under a major shake-up of the pass system. Under the new rules, two MPs will need to sign for a lobbyist to register for a pass, with the primary sponsor responsible for their behaviour. It will also introduce fees for lobbyist and commercial passes. A letter, seen by Guardian Australia, will be distributed to federal parliamentarians on Thursday morning detailing the new rules.

In their letter to parliamentarians, Dick and Lines said they were committed to “maintaining the democratic openness of Parliament House, while ensuring that access to the private areas is appropriately managed, transparent, and aligned with community expectations”. “The revised policy strengthens the transparency and oversight of access passes issued to individuals who have privileged access to Parliament House,” the letter states. Their review has also determined new categories for sponsored passes – with political lobbyists to remain with orange passes, while commercial representatives and advocacy and community groups are to apply for light blue passes. Commercial and community passes will now include the organisation and names of the sponsoring MPs, individual names will not appear on the register. Access passes for former parliamentarians from states and territory legislatures will be now be restricted to former premiers, chief ministers and ministers.

The changes drastically increase the transparency of the pass system, under which the public currently has no knowledge of who has sponsored a lobbyist pass, or how many passes an MP has sponsored. There were more than 2,050 sponsored passes for access to Parliament House as of mid-2024. It’s unknown how many of those were held by paid lobbyists. The review of the policies governing access to the building’s private areas was conducted by the House speaker, Milton Dick and Senate president, Sue Lines. The prime minister wrote to them in March ahead of the review and suggested greater “transparency and rigour” of sponsored pass holders.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
MPs who sponsor lobbyists’ entry to halls of power will also be listed online under new transparency rules

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Political lobbyists with unfettered access to the halls of Parliament House – and the MPs who sponsor their passes – will soon be publicly identified in an online register, under a major shake-up of the pass system.

Under the new rules, two MPs will need to sign for a lobbyist to register for a pass, with the primary sponsor responsible for their behaviour. It will also introduce fees for lobbyist and commercial passes.

A letter, seen by Guardian Australia, will be distributed to federal parliamentarians on Thursday morning detailing the new rules.

The changes drastically increase the transparency of the pass system, under which the public currently has no knowledge of who has sponsored a lobbyist pass, or how many passes an MP has sponsored.

There were more than 2,050 sponsored passes for access to Parliament House as of mid-2024. It’s unknown how many of those were held by paid lobbyists.

The review of the policies governing access to the building’s private areas was conducted by the House speaker, Milton Dick and Senate president, Sue Lines. The prime minister wrote to them in March ahead of the review and suggested greater “transparency and rigour” of sponsored pass holders.

In their letter to parliamentarians, Dick and Lines said they were committed to “maintaining the democratic openness of Parliament House, while ensuring that access to the private areas is appropriately managed, transparent, and aligned with community expectations”.

“The revised policy strengthens the transparency and oversight of access passes issued to individuals who have privileged access to Parliament House,” the letter states.

Their review has also determined new categories for sponsored passes – with political lobbyists to remain with orange passes, while commercial representatives and advocacy and community groups are to apply for light blue passes.

Commercial and community passes will now include the organisation and names of the sponsoring MPs, individual names will not appear on the register.

Access passes for former parliamentarians from states and territory legislatures will be now be restricted to former premiers, chief ministers and ministers.

Visitors with orange passes currently have rights to unescorted access to the non-public area

payload.title: Australian parlamentin lobbaripassit tuodaan julkiseen rekisteriin
payload.summary: Australian parlamenttitalon kulkulupajärjestelmää uudistetaan. Jatkossa poliittiset lobbarit ja heidän passinsa sponsoroineet kansanedustajat nimetään julkisessa verkkorekisterissä.
payload.content:
Australian parlamenttitalon kulkulupajärjestelmää uudistetaan niin, että poliittiset lobbarit, joilla on etuoikeutettu pääsy parlamenttitalon tiloihin, nimetään jatkossa julkisessa verkkorekisterissä. Rekisteriin merkitään myös ne kansanedustajat, jotka ovat sponsoroineet lobbarien passit. Uusista säännöistä kerrotaan liittoparlamentaarikoille torstaina jaettavassa kirjeessä.

## Sponsorointi muuttuu tiukemmaksi

Uudistuksen mukaan lobbarin passihakemusta varten tarvitaan jatkossa kahden kansanedustajan hyväksyntä. Ensisijainen sponsori on vastuussa sponsoroimansa henkilön käytöksestä parlamenttitalossa. Muutoksen yhteydessä otetaan käyttöön myös maksuja lobbaripasseille ja kaupallisille passeille.

Tähän asti yleisöllä ei ole ollut tietoa siitä, kuka on sponsoroinut lobbaripassin tai kuinka monta passia yksittäinen kansanedustaja on sponsoroinut. Vuoden 2024 puolivälissä parlamenttitaloon oli yli 2 050 sponsoroitua kulkulupaa. Ei ole tiedossa, kuinka moni niistä oli palkattujen lobbarien hallussa.

## Uudet passiluokat erotellaan

Parlamenttitalon yksityisten alueiden kulkusääntöjen arvioinnin tekivät edustajainhuoneen puhemies Milton Dick ja senaatin puhemies Sue Lines. Pääministeri oli kirjoittanut heille maaliskuussa ennen arviointia ja ehdottanut lisää läpinäkyvyyttä ja kurinalaisuutta sponsoroitujen passien haltijoihin.

Uudessa käytännössä poliittiset lobbarit pysyvät oranssien passien piirissä. Kaupallisten edustajien sekä edunvalvonta- ja yhteisöryhmien on puolestaan haettava vaaleansinisiä passeja. Kaupallisten ja yhteisöpassien rekisteriin merkitään organisaatio sekä sponsoroivien kansanedustajien nimet, mutta yksittäisten passinhaltijoiden nimiä ei julkaista.

## Tavoitteena avoimuus ja valvonta

Kirjeen mukaan tavoitteena on säilyttää parlamenttitalon demokraattinen avoimuus ja samalla varmistaa, että pääsy yksityisille alueille on asianmukaisesti hallittua, läpinäkyvää ja yleisön odotusten mukaista. Kirjeessä todetaan myös, että uudistettu käytäntö vahvistaa niiden kulkulupien läpinäkyvyyttä ja valvontaa, jotka antavat haltijoilleen erityisen pääsyn parlamenttitaloon.

Muutokset rajaavat myös osavaltioiden ja territorioiden entisten parlamentaarikkojen kulkulupia. Jatkossa niitä saavat entisistä alueellisista päättäjistä vain entiset pääministerit, hallintoalueiden johtajat ja ministerit.
